pictures.scene: Ilya Repin, Religious Procession in Kursk Province — the whole countryside walking out together behind the icon and the banners in the dust and the heat, a psalm, a song for the Sabbath day, it is good to praise the LORD
pictures.name: pd_repin_loven

pictures.scene: Claude Lorrain, Seaport with the Embarkation of the Queen of Sheba — the sun standing low over the water between the palaces while the boats are loaded at the quay, and to sing praises to Your name, O Most High, to proclaim Your loving devotion in the morning
pictures.name: pd_lorrain_morgen

pictures.scene: Adam Elsheimer, The Flight into Egypt — the family going on through the dark under the whole starry sky with the fire burning low beside the water, and Your faithfulness at night, with the ten-stringed harp
pictures.name: pd_elsheimer_nacht

pictures.scene: Henry Ossawa Tanner, The Banjo Lesson — the old man holding the instrument steady while the boy's hands find the strings, and the melody of the lyre, for You, O LORD, have made me glad by Your deeds
pictures.name: pd_tanner_snaren

pictures.scene: Frederic Edwin Church, The Icebergs — the green and white walls of ice standing up out of the still sea in the cold light, I sing for joy at the works of Your hands, how great are Your works, O LORD
pictures.name: pd_church_werken

pictures.scene: Johan Christian Dahl, View from Stalheim — the valley opening away below the crags with the rainbow standing over the far mountains, how deep are Your thoughts, a senseless man does not know
pictures.name: pd_dahl_gedachten

pictures.scene: Quentin Massys, Ill-Matched Lovers — the grinning old man taken in by the woman while the accomplice lifts his purse behind his back, and a fool does not understand, that though the wicked sprout like grass
pictures.name: pd_massys_dwaas

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, Dulle Griet — the whole burning landscape of plunder and greed with the looters at their work before the mouth of hell, and all evildoers flourish, they will be forever destroyed
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_vernietigd

pictures.scene: Giovanni Battista Gaulli, The Triumph of the Name of Jesus — the blazing name of Jesus opened in the height of heaven with the saints rising into the light around it, but You, O LORD, are exalted forever, for surely Your enemies, O LORD
pictures.name: pd_gaulli_verheven

pictures.scene: Philips Wouwerman, Ruitergevecht — the horsemen breaking apart in the smoke with riders going down under the hooves, surely Your enemies will perish, all evildoers will be scattered
pictures.name: pd_wouwerman_verstrooid

pictures.scene: Claude Lorrain, David sacré roi par le prophète Samuel — the prophet pouring the horn of oil over the bowed head of the shepherd boy leaning on his staff, but You have exalted my horn like that of a wild ox, with fine oil I have been anointed
pictures.name: pd_lorrain_gezalfd

pictures.scene: Raphael, The Expulsion of Heliodorus from the Temple — the horseman riding the plunderer down on the temple floor with the stolen gold spilling out of its vessel and the men crying out around him, my eyes see the downfall of my enemies, my ears hear the wailing of my wicked foes
pictures.name: pd_raphael_ogen

pictures.scene: Tivadar Csontváry Kosztka, Pilgrimage to the Cedars of Lebanon — the great cedar standing over the white mountains with the pilgrims dancing in a ring under its branches, the righteous will flourish like a palm tree, and grow like a cedar in Lebanon
pictures.name: pd_csontvary_ceder

pictures.scene: John Constable, Salisbury Cathedral from the Bishop's Grounds — the spire standing up out of the green close with the old trees planted around it and the cattle at the water, planted in the house of the LORD, they will flourish in the courts of our God
pictures.name: pd_constable_geplant

pictures.scene: Vincent van Gogh, Olive Trees — the old knotted trunks still carrying their whole weight of green and blue leaves over the bright ground, in old age they will still bear fruit, healthy and green they will remain
pictures.name: pd_vangogh_vrucht

pictures.scene: Alexandre Calame, Bei Handeck — the one fir standing straight on the mountainside under the great pale wall of rock, to proclaim, the LORD is upright, He is my Rock, and in Him there is no unrighteousness
pictures.name: pd_calame_rots

lines.text: A Psalm. A song for the Sabbath day.
It is good to praise the LORD,
and to sing praises to Your name, O Most High,
to proclaim Your loving devotion in the morning
and Your faithfulness at night
with the ten-stringed harp
and the melody of the lyre.
For You, O LORD, have made me glad by Your deeds;
I sing for joy at the works of Your hands.
How great are Your works, O LORD,
how deep are Your thoughts!
A senseless man does not know,
and a fool does not understand,
that though the wicked sprout like grass,
and all evildoers flourish,
they will be forever destroyed.
But You, O LORD, are exalted forever!
For surely Your enemies, O LORD,
surely Your enemies will perish;
all evildoers will be scattered.
But You have exalted my horn like that of a wild ox;
with fine oil I have been anointed.
My eyes see the downfall of my enemies;
my ears hear the wailing of my wicked foes.
The righteous will flourish like a palm tree,
and grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
Planted in the house of the LORD,
they will flourish in the courts of our God.
In old age they will still bear fruit;
healthy and green they will remain,
to proclaim, “The LORD is upright; He is my Rock,
and in Him there is no unrighteousness.”
